title: LDAP password confirmation fails when saving Global Credentials
body: I log in to Nextcloud with an LDAP account. In Personal settings, when I enter a new password in Global Credentials and save it, Nextcloud asks me to confirm my account password. Even when I enter the correct password, confirmation fails and the POST to apps/files_external/globalcredentials returns HTTP 403. This is on Nextcloud 31.0.2.1 with Apache, PHP 8.2, MariaDB, OpenLDAP, Redis/APCu, and encryption disabled.

symptoms_visible: When I save a new Global Credentials password, Nextcloud asks me to confirm my LDAP account password, rejects the correct password, and the request to apps/files_external/globalcredentials returns HTTP 403.
N0.label: N0 LDAP password confirmation failure reported

symptoms_visible: The correct LDAP password is still rejected when I try to save Global Credentials.
N1.label: N1 server and Apache setup confirmed

symptoms_visible: With the temporary diagnostic edit applied, the request returns HTTP 500 instead of 403, and the password shown locally in the diagnostic output is the password I entered.
N2.label: N2 password transport checked

symptoms_visible: After setting PHP-FPM clear_env to no, Nextcloud still rejects the correct password confirmation.
N2_x.label: N2_x PHP-FPM environment change aftermath

symptoms_visible: The confirmation request still fails; Nextcloud logs a login failure for my internal Nextcloud UUID, and the LDAP server receives a search that places that UUID into the configured login-attribute filter.
N3.label: N3 incorrect LDAP lookup identifier exposed

symptoms_visible: After checking the proposed server change, the issue is resolved for me.
N4.label: N4 proposed server fix verified

symptoms_visible: I can complete the sensitive Global Credentials action without the correct LDAP password being rejected.
N_terminal.label: terminal LDAP confirmation resolved

question_patterns: Can you describe the server setup and whether a reverse proxy is involved?
Are you using Apache or nginx, and is Nextcloud behind a proxy?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Nextcloud is installed on a physical Dell PowerEdge running Debian 12.10. I use Apache 2 with PHP 8.2-FPM, and there is no reverse proxy. Users authenticate through OpenLDAP.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am behind a reverse proxy that strips the Authorization header before the request reaches Nextcloud.
The same setup uses PHP 8.3-FPM instead of PHP 8.2-FPM.

question_patterns: Can you confirm whether Apache's mod_env module is enabled?
What does sudo a2enmod env report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Running sudo a2enmod env reports: Module env already enabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: mod_env was disabled, and enabling it makes password confirmation work.

edges.comment: Opening reporter reporter, c1 and c4: this edge contains only the reporter's physical Debian/Apache/PHP-FPM/OpenLDAP setup and the requested mod_env check. Other participants' nginx, proxy, OIDC, and built-in-auth setups are not merged into this reporter's causal chain.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily apply this diagnostic edit, inspect the resulting log only on your own server, and confirm whether the decoded password matches what you entered?
Please use the temporary middleware diagnostic, do not post the sensitive output, and tell me only whether the password was retrieved correctly.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I applied the diagnostic edit. The password on the auth object line is correct, the data password is correct, and I can confirm that my account password is correct in the local log. The request returns HTTP 500 with the diagnostic exception.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The locally decoded password is empty or different from what I entered.
The password matches, but the temporary diagnostic exception is displayed in a different browser.

edges.comment: reporter c14-c15, prompted by c13: the temporary edit is a diagnostic measurement and was explicitly to be reverted. The reporter discloses only that the locally inspected values match, not the password or authorization header. The engineer's conclusion that header transport is not the problem appears later and is not put into the user's answer.

solution.intent: Make PHP-FPM expose inherited environment variables by setting clear_env to no, in case the confirmation failure is caused by the FPM environment configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Set clear_env = no in the PHP-FPM pool configuration, restart PHP-FPM, and retry the Global Credentials action.

edges.comment: reporter c27-c28: the reporter tested clear_env = no and said it did not correct the problem. The earlier diagnostic had already shown that Nextcloud received the entered password correctly.

question_patterns: Does nextcloud.log contain a login-failed entry when you submit the confirmation dialog?
What non-sensitive identifier appears in the login failure for the confirmation request?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. nextcloud.log reports a login failure during the POST to /apps/files_external/globalcredentials, and the quoted username is my Nextcloud UUID rather than the login name I normally use.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no login-failed entry; the request fails before any authentication attempt is logged.

question_patterns: Do the LDAP server logs show a related search or bind failure when you confirm the password?
What value is Nextcloud putting into your configured LDAP login-attribute search?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the LDAP log, I see a search over uid, mail, and supannAliasLogin, but Nextcloud supplies my Nextcloud UUID as the value. That search fails; users normally log in with their login, short login, or mail address.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The LDAP log shows a successful search for my normal login name followed by a failed bind using the entered password.
The same UUID is searched against a slightly different set of configured login attributes.

edges.comment: reporter c31 in response to c30: these are the reporter's redacted raw Nextcloud and slapd observations. The OIDC investigation and built-in-user reports are separate sub-problems and are deliberately excluded.

question_patterns: Could you check whether the linked change addresses your issue?
Please test the linked change on your affected LDAP setup and tell me whether the problem remains.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked it, and for me the issue is resolved. Thank you for the help.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I tested the linked change, but the same correct LDAP password is still rejected.

edges.comment: reporter c33 responding to artong c32, which linked PR 51870. This is pre-landing verification of the linked change by the opening reporter. The reporter stated only that the issue was resolved; no unreported code-level behavior is attributed to them.

solution.intent: Adopt the tested server-side correction for LDAP password confirmation rather than changing Apache, PHP-FPM, or the reporter's LDAP password scheme.
solution.concrete_example: Use the server change offered in PR 51870, which the affected LDAP reporter tested and reported as resolving the issue, then verify the Global Credentials action on the affected instance.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence shows that the password reached the middleware correctly, while the confirmation check generated an LDAP search using the internal Nextcloud UUID in place of a usable login identifier. Connecting those observations into the password-confirmation root cause is engineer-side inference; the linked PR's unquoted implementation details must not be invented.

edges.comment: Resolution of the opening reporter's LDAP chain: c31 identifies the failed UUID-based LDAP search, c32 offers a server PR, and c33 confirms that it resolves reporter's case. Later OIDC and built-in-auth discussions describe different deployments and are not folded into this resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause for the opening LDAP case: password confirmation receives the correct password but attempts the LDAP lookup using the user's internal Nextcloud UUID rather than a usable configured login identifier.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the local diagnostic result, the Nextcloud login-failed entry, and the LDAP search log rather than inferred from the HTTP 403 alone.

Must not treat missing Apache mod_env, a reverse proxy, or PHP-FPM clear_env as the fix: mod_env was enabled, there was no reverse proxy, the password arrived correctly, and clear_env = no did not resolve the failure.
Must recommend the tested server-side correction for LDAP password confirmation rather than changing the LDAP password hash scheme or asking the user to keep retrying the same password.

Must ask the affected user to verify the sensitive action on a build containing the server-side fix before declaring resolution; the opening reporter did verify the proposed change and reported the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced system administrator who operates a physical Debian Nextcloud server with Apache, PHP-FPM, OpenLDAP, MariaDB, Redis, and APCu; comfortable editing a PHP file temporarily and reading redacted application and slapd logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, cooperative, and methodical. Provides concrete command output and log excerpts, protects sensitive password data, proposes infrastructure hypotheses cautiously, and thanks maintainers when the tested change resolves the issue.
